{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABYkU7tQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhCJMA4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 23, "title": "Implement complete classic Konami SCC wavetable audio for MegaROM cartridges", "body": "## Problem

The existing `Konami SCC` MegaROM mapper correctly implements ROM bank switching and detects SCC activation when bank 3Fh is selected in the third switchable bank window, but its 9800h–9FFFh SCC memory overlay currently reads FFh and ignores writes. No SCC waveform RAM, frequency/volume/enable registers, oscillator, or audio samples exist. As a result, SCC-equipped games cannot reproduce their expected music or sound effects, and some software that reads SCC registers may behave incorrectly despite a valid ROM mapping.

The goal is to complete **classic Konami SCC (K051649) sound hardware** within the existing MSX1/MSX2 emulator, rather than introducing an unrelated SCC+ / SCC-I cartridge or FM sound implementation.

## Expected outcome

An MSX1 or MSX2 Konami SCC cartridge can enable the SCC overlay through its existing bank register, read/write the documented classic SCC registers, and generate five independent oscillator voices (with channels 4 and 5 sharing waveform data) using real emulated Z80 memory accesses. SCC output is mixed into the existing browser/Wasm audio stream alongside the AY-3-8910 PSG, including working audio mute/reset/ejection behavior.

No proprietary Konami game ROM, BIOS or sound asset is shipped. The sound implementation and original tests are written independently from public hardware documentation; do not copy existing GPL emulator implementations.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository `takahirox/msx-rust` on `main` (last checked `e8ee30ad09ac`). Relevant code: `crates/msx-core/src/cartridge.rs`, `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/msx-core/src/psg.rs`, `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `web/app.js`, and existing cartridge/PSG/browser tests.
- `Mapping::write` already enables the Konami SCC overlay when bank 3Fh is selected via the mapped 9000h–97FFh register range. `Mapping::read` currently returns FFh across 9800h–9FFFh while enabled; `Hardware::write` sends all cartridge writes only to the mapper. Audio samples currently come only from `Psg::tick` and are exposed as a single audio buffer to Wasm.
- Related work: #8 (MegaROM mappers), #13 (Auto inference), #15 and #19 (bundled model-specific C-BIOS and firmware policy), #21 (redistributable demo ROMs).
- Public hardware references, to interpret and cross-check independently:
  - https://www.msx.org/wiki/MegaROM_Mappers and https://www.msx.org/wiki/Konami_051649 (MSX Wiki; exact pages may have alternate paths)
  - https://ngs.no.coocan.jp/doc/wiki.cgi?page=SCC+Sound+Chip (register windows and classic channel 4/5 wave sharing)
  - https://direct.msx.org/wiki/ROM_mappers (mapper/SCC enable and register map)
- The original K051649 has **five playable voices**, **four sets of 32 signed 8-bit waveform samples**, a **12-bit frequency register** and **4-bit volume** per voice, and a channel on/off bitmask. Channels 4/5 share wave storage. This differs from SCC+ / K052539, which is out of scope unless independently necessary to validate classic SCC behavior.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Correct classic SCC registers and cartridge gating

- [ ] Add a focused classic SCC hardware implementation in the Rust core with deterministic initial/reset state: shared waveform RAM, five oscillator/frequency counters, per-channel 12-bit frequencies, 4-bit volumes, enable mask and applicable standard test/deformation-register behavior. Document any documented undefined/analog behavior approximations; do not claim chip-perfect analog reproduction.
- [ ] Correctly memory-map the classic SCC registers (waveform region 9800h–987Fh; five frequencies 9880h–9889h; volumes 988Ah–988Eh; channel enables 988Fh; applicable mirrors/other documented registers in the 9800h–9FFFh overlay). Match documented read/write/open-bus behavior, including channel 4/5 waveform sharing and reserved/read-only regions. Do not invent read-back values for write-only registers.
- [ ] Integrate SCC overlay access through the **currently selected Konami SCC cartridge slot only**. Selecting bank 3Fh in the appropriate mapper register must expose the SCC; leaving that bank must disable its overlay and restore ordinary ROM visibility and mapper behavior. Writes to ordinary ROM addresses must not accidentally alter sound registers. When overlay is disabled or the cartridge slot is not mapped, SCC must neither intercept memory accesses nor continue erroneously generating cartridge audio. Preserve normal bank selection and the existing slot/mirror/reset rules.
- [ ] Ensure SCC state is correctly reinitialized on Reset, Eject, cartridge replacement, switching between MSX1/MSX2, firmware changes and failed/successful ROM imports. Failed imports must not corrupt the active cartridge, mapper, SCC voices/wave RAM or PSG state. When a supported cartridge is reloaded, old waveforms or tones must not leak into the new session.

### Timing and sound integration

- [ ] Generate five SCC wavetable voices from emulated CPU-cycle timing with per-channel independent pitch, frequency updates and looping 32-sample waveforms. Use signed sample interpretation, channel enable/disable and volume changes as specified; include reasonable, documented handling of zero frequency, frequency counter resets, and classic SCC deformation/test modes. Make timing deterministic and avoid frame-bound pitch drift.
- [ ] Mix the emulated SCC into the existing 44.1 kHz mono audio path **alongside the PSG**, preserving PCM buffer length and the Wasm/browser ABI; ensure neither the existing PSG tone/noise/envelope tests nor muted/silenced buffers regress. Apply bounded gain/headroom so concurrent PSG + SCC audio does not cause severe clipping or invalid/NaN samples.
- [ ] Preserve browser user-gesture audio activation, `Enable audio`/`Mute audio`/`Resume audio`, pause/reset and focus-loss behavior. No new audio libraries, runtime network requests, persistent recorded assets or browser-specific code in `msx-core` are required.

### Automated validation and compatible UX

- [ ] Add comprehensive, independently authored Rust unit/integration tests for the exact SCC memory/register map, wave RAM writes and readback, fifth-voice wave sharing, channel independence, frequencies/volumes/mute mask, test-register behavior, memory overlay activation/deactivation, slot masking, mapper bank changes and transactional reset/ejection/replacement.
- [ ] Create original, redistributable **Konami SCC MegaROM fixture(s)** that execute Z80 code on the emulated MSX1 and MSX2, select the SCC bank, program nonzero distinct waveforms and frequency/volume registers, and demonstrate SCC playback plus simultaneous PSG. Do not use any commercial music or copyrighted game-ROM bytes; validate against independently calculated expected waveform/frequency/sample properties instead of copying third-party emulator code.
- [ ] Add Playwright tests exercising the real compiled Wasm + browser audio path: import/boot the fixture with `Konami SCC` selected and (where inference is sufficiently supported) `Auto`, verify generated nonzero/finite SCC samples with correct transitions to silence when disabled, verify PSG still works and both can sound together, verify browser mute/reset/Eject, and retain full MSX1/MSX2 cartridge and demo regressions. Automated waveform assertions are mandatory; physical speaker listening is not.
- [ ] Update README, detailed SCC mapper documentation, user-facing advanced-options text and compatibility claims to explain **classic SCC audio support**, the separate Konami Standard vs Konami SCC choices, any genuine accuracy limits, and continued lack of SCC+/SCC-I, SRAM and unrelated MSX audio expansions. Do not confuse correct mapper import with guaranteed commercial-game compatibility.
- [ ] Run and report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test`, and other directly relevant automated checks. Preserve the current static GitHub Pages deployment, C-BIOS license notices, privacy, Weave BASIC, the demo gallery and existing tests.
- [ ] Follow the repository's Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision → merge process. **All mandatory pre-merge conditions must be AI-verifiable**; no user-provided game ROM, subjective hearing check or physical MSX confirmation may block merge. Do not add speculative unrelated sound chips or unnecessary framework changes.

## Optional validation

After merge, the owner can try lawfully acquired classic Konami SCC games (for example, Gradius/Nemesis 2 or Parodius) and compare music/effects against real MSX hardware or a reference emulator. Track newly observed gameplay/audio incompatibilities as separate follow-up Issues; these subjective tests are not pre-merge approval conditions.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] Verify the merged build has been deployed to https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ through the successful main GitHub Pages run. On the published site, import a redistributable original SCC test cartridge and verify that the actual Wasm/audio path produces nonzero SCC audio samples, alongside PSG, and returns to silence on mute/ejection; record the deployment URL/run/observed result. Do this only **after merge** and open a separate Issue if the live site fails.
